---
title: Add a mail driver
description: Send Pluto emails through a provider other than Resend.
navigation:
  icon: i-lucide-send
---

A mail driver is a small object. It sends one message through one provider. You register it on the server.

## The contract

```ts
interface PlutoMailDriver {
  /** The value of NUXT_PLUTO_MAIL_DRIVER that selects this driver. */
  id: string
  /** False when the driver cannot send yet. The default is true. */
  isConfigured?: () => boolean
  send: (message: PlutoMailMessage, context: PlutoMailSendContext) => Promise<PlutoMailSendResult>
}
```

- `PlutoMailMessage` has `to`, `subject`, `html`, `text`, and the optional `from`, `replyTo`, and `idempotencyKey`.
- `PlutoMailSendContext` has the configured `from` and `replyTo`. They can be empty.
- `PlutoMailSendResult` is `{ id, driver }`.

## Step 1: write the driver

```ts [server/mail/my-provider.ts]
export const myProviderDriver: PlutoMailDriver = {
  id: 'my-provider',
  isConfigured: () => Boolean(useRuntimeConfig().myProvider?.apiKey),
  async send(message, context) {
    const response = await fetch('https://api.example.com/send', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${useRuntimeConfig().myProvider.apiKey}` },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        from: message.from || context.from,
        to: message.to,
        subject: message.subject,
        html: message.html,
        text: message.text
      })
    })
    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new PlutoMailError('provider_error', 'The provider failed to send the message.', { status: response.status })
    }
    return { id: null, driver: 'my-provider' }
  }
}
```

The example reads the key from a private `runtimeConfig.myProvider.apiKey` value. Declare it in the `nuxt.config.ts` of your layer with an empty default. Then the variable `NUXT_MY_PROVIDER_API_KEY` sets it at run time.

Follow these rules:

- Throw a `PlutoMailError` on failure. It takes the error code, a fixed English message, and optional `status` and `providerCode` values. See [Mail](/core/mail) for the codes.
- Never log a recipient, a subject, a link, or a key. Never put them in an error message.
- Read a secret only on the server.
- Keep secrets in the environment.

## Step 2: register the driver

Register the driver when the server starts:

```ts [server/plugins/mail.ts]
export default defineNitroPlugin(() => {
  registerMailDriver(myProviderDriver)
})
```

## Step 3: select the driver

Set the driver id in the environment of the running server:

```bash [.env]
NUXT_PLUTO_MAIL_DRIVER=my-provider
```

If the id is not registered, Pluto uses the `none` driver and logs one warning. In production, Pluto never falls back to the `dev` driver.

## Step 4: test the driver

Tests never call a real provider. Pass a fake `fetch`, or stub `globalThis.fetch`. Add a test for each error code that your driver can throw.

## Optional: a mail store

A `PlutoMailStore` is a source of secrets other than the environment. It has an `id` and a `get(name)` function. The only name today is `'resendApiKey'`, so a store cannot give the secrets of your own driver. A backend layer can register one with `registerMailStore`. The environment always wins over a store. Read the secrets of your own driver from the environment.

## Optional: an Email page section

Explain your provider setup in **Settings, Email** with a `mailPanels` entry. The guided setup of that page covers Resend only. Register the panel component with `defineAsyncComponent`. See [Mail](/core/mail).
